Evaluating that end-to-end requires a fixture audit with ~10 FROMs spanning all five classification classes plus no-action-needed; the eval rubric for ordering, summary-panel correctness, and per-FROM precedence-resolution becomes a sprawling weighted_checklist (~25+ items) that's hard to score reliably. infeasible_scenarios.scenario: Cross-classification ambiguity: a bump that legitimately matches two categories
infeasible_scenarios.reasoning: The rubric documents precedence resolution (e.g. license-aware beats safe-mechanical for RHEL UBI majors — covered by rhel-ubi-license-aware). A more synthetic test, e.g. an alpine:edge → alpine:edge `requires-migration AND not-recommended` ambiguity, is contrived enough that real-world advice doesn't depend on it. The single-precedence-rule scenarios in rhel-ubi-license-aware (license-aware over safe-mechanical) and alpine-edge-not-recommended (not-recommended over anything) cover the precedence behaviour without needing a multi-conflict synthetic case.
